record.paper_title: Ball-Evans approximation problem: recent progress and open problems
record.context_brief: Jacobian sign for continuous open discrete maps
record.original_question: Let n ≥ 3 and let p satisfy floor(n/2) < p ≤ n−1, or 1 ≤ p ≤ 2 when n = 3. Suppose Ω ⊂ R^n is connected and f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω, R^n) is continuous, open, and discrete. Is it possible that both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} have positive measure?

evidence.quote: The usual way how to prove that the mapping f : Ω → R^n in question is in fact a homeomorphism is to first show that it is continuous, open (maps open sets to open sets) and discrete (preimage of single point does not have an accumulation point in Ω).

Open problem 11. Sign of the Jacobian for continuous, open and discrete mappings: Let n ≥ 3 and [n/2] < p ≤ n−1 (or 1 ≤ p ≤ 2 for n = 3). Let Ω ⊂ R^n be connected open set and let f ∈ W1,p(Ω, R^n) be a continuous, open and discrete mapping. Is it possible that both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} have positive measure?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer and let $p$ be a real number satisfying $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor < p \leq n-1$, or, in the special case $n = 3$, satisfying $1 \leq p \leq 2$. Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a connected open set, and let $f \in W^{1,p}(\Omega, \mathbb{R}^n)$ be a mapping that is

(i) continuous,
(ii) open (i.e., $f$ maps open subsets of $\Omega$ to open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$), and
(iii) discrete (i.e., for every $y \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the preimage $f^{-1}(y)$ has no accumulation point in $\Omega$).

Denote by $J_f(x) = \det Df(x)$ the Jacobian determinant of $f$, defined almost everywhere via the weak derivative. Determine whether it is possible that both of the sets
$$\{x \in \Omega : J_f(x) > 0\} \quad \text{and} \quad \{x \in \Omega : J_f(x) < 0\}$$
have positive Lebesgue measure.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on the Ball–Evans approximation problem. The analogous question for Sobolev homeomorphisms in the same range of $p$ has been answered (the Jacobian cannot change sign), but for the broader class of continuous, open, discrete Sobolev mappings the problem remains unresolved, since standard degree-theoretic and linking-number arguments used in the homeomorphism case do not apply.

status_evidence.title: Ball-Evans approximation problem: recent progress and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem 11. Sign of the Jacobian for continuous, open and discrete mappings...
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly stated as an open problem in a 2025 survey.

status_evidence.title: Jacobians of W^{1,p} homeomorphisms, case p=[n/2]
status_evidence.snippet: Jacobians of Sobolev homeomorphisms cannot change sign for p > [n/2].
status_evidence.claim: The corresponding result is known for homeomorphisms, but the question for continuous open discrete maps is distinct and unresolved.
